'''John Allen Henson''' (born December 28, 1990) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who played eight seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina Tar Heels]], where he was a two-time [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] Defensive Player of the Year.<ref name="thb">{{cite news|title=John Henson Biography|url=http://www.goheels.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=205497517|access-date=October 2, 2015|work=GoHeels.com}}</ref> Henson was selected with the 14th overall pick in [[2012 NBA draft]] by the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] and played his first {{frac|6|1|2}} seasons with the team before being traded to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in December 2018. In February 2020, he was traded to the [[Detroit Pistons]].

==High school career==
For three years, Henson attended [[Round Rock High School]] in [[Round Rock, Texas]].<ref name="thb" /> His senior year, Henson transferred to [[Sickles High School]] in [[Tampa, Florida]]. Henson wore the jersey number 33, averaging 17.6 points, 12.2 rebounds, and 6.1 blocks per game as a senior in 2008–09. He scored a season-high 29 points against [[Tampa Bay Technical High School|Tampa Bay Tech]] and blocked 10 or more shots five times with a high of 11 on four occasions as a senior as well.<ref name="thb" /> Henson led the team to a 24–5 record and a perfect 10–0 league record,<ref>{{cite news|title=John Henson's (Tampa, FL) High School Basketball Stats|url=http://www.maxpreps.com/athlete/john-henson/J4CxqvTrEeKZ5AAmVebBJg/gendersport/basketball-stats.htm#year=08-09|access-date=October 2, 2015|work=MaxPreps.com}}</ref> but the team lost to [[Lakeland Senior High School (Lakeland, Florida)|Lakeland]] 48–43 in the regional semi-finals for the Florida FHSAA Class 6A championship.<ref>{{cite news|title=2009 Allstate FHSAA Class 6A Boys Basketball Championship|url=http://www.fhsaa.org/sites/default/files/orig_uploads/sports/basketball-boys/archives/2008-09/brak6.htm|access-date=October 2, 2015|work=FHSAA.org|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120722230013/http://www.fhsaa.org/sites/default/files/orig_uploads/sports/basketball-boys/archives/2008-09/brak6.htm|archive-date=July 22, 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref> Henson was a first-team all-state selection and Tampa Bay Coaches Association Player of the Year. He played in the [[McDonald's All-American Game]] and the [[Nike Hoop Summit]]. He also earned first-team [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]] honors.<ref name="thb" />

===Recruiting===
Henson was a highly sought-after forward and was rated by [[Scout.com]] as the #1 power forward and the #4 overall player in the 2009 recruiting class.<ref>{{cite news|title=SCOUT.COM COLLEGE BASKETBALL TEAM RECRUITING PROSPECTS – 2009|url=http://scouthoops.scout.com/a.z?s=75&p=9&c=4&cfg=bb&yr=2009|access-date=October 2, 2015|work=Scout.com}}</ref> Analysts predicted he would be an important addition to what some thought would be the best front court in the nation for the 2009–10 season. When asked to evaluate Henson, head coach [[Roy Williams (coach)|Roy Williams]] said Henson had "tremendously long arms" and predicted he would "probably block more shots than any perimeter player in college basketball."<ref>{{cite news|title=Season Preview: 2009-10 North Carolina Tar Heels|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/273402-season-preview-2009-10-north-carolina-tar-heels|access-date=October 2, 2015|work=BleacherReport.com|date=October 17, 2009}}</ref>

==College career==
[[File:John Henson cropped.jpg|thumb|right|upright|Henson with the Tar Heels in November 2011|130px]]
At the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]], Henson began as a small forward for the [[2009–10 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|2009–10 Tar Heels]], but with the season-ending injury to [[Ed Davis (basketball)|Ed Davis]], Henson moved to power forward in mid-February 2010. After the move, Henson's performance improved, and he averaged 9.4 points per game in the last 16 contests of the season.<ref name="thb" /> However, the Tar Heels missed the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|NCAA tournament]], losing to the [[Dayton Flyers men's basketball|Dayton Flyers]] in the [[National Invitation Tournament|NIT]] finals.<ref>{{cite news|title=Dayton wins first NIT title since 1968 by stopping UNC's run|url=http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/recap/_/id/300912168/boxscore?gameId=300912168|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141024111205/http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/recap/_/id/300912168/boxscore?gameId=300912168|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 24, 2014|access-date=October 2, 2015|work=ESPN.com|date=April 1, 2010}}</ref>

As a sophomore in the 2010–11 season, Henson was the winner of the ACC Defensive Player of the Year award for 2011 after averaging 11.7 points, 10.1 rebounds and 3.2 blocks per game. As a junior in 2011–12, he was again named the ACC Defensive Player of the Year after averaging 13.7 points, 9.9 rebounds and 2.9 blocks per game.<ref name="thb" />

On March 29, 2012, he declared for the [[NBA draft]], forgoing his final year of college eligibility.<ref>{{cite news|title=Three UNC stars to enter NBA draft|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2012/story/_/id/7752253/north-carolina-tar-heels-john-henson-harrison-barnes-kendall-marshall-enter-draft|access-date=October 2, 2015|work=ESPN.com|date=March 29, 2012}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Milwaukee Bucks (2012–2018)===
[[File:John Henson John Wall.jpg|thumb|Henson with the Bucks in March 2013, greeting [[John Wall]] of the Washington Wizards]]
On June 28, 2012, Henson was selected with the 14th overall pick in the [[2012 NBA draft]] by the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].<ref>{{cite news|title=John Henson To Bucks With No. 14 Pick In 2012 NBA Draft|url=http://www.huffingtonpost.com/2012/06/28/john-henson-milwaukee-bucks-unc-draft-pick_n_1636125.html|access-date=October 2, 2015|work=HuffingtonPost.com|date=June 28, 2012}}</ref> On July 10, 2012, he signed his rookie scale contract with the Bucks.<ref>{{cite news|title=Bucks sign forward John Henson|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/8154405/milwaukee-bucks-sign-first-round-pick-john-henson|access-date=October 2, 2015|work=ESPN.com|date=July 10, 2012}}</ref> On April 10, 2013, he had a season-best game with 17 points, 25 rebounds and seven blocks in a 113–103 loss to the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Notebook: Magic 113, Bucks 103|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20130410/MILORL/gameinfo.html|access-date=October 2, 2015|work=NBA.com|date=April 10, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140322013726/http://www.nba.com/games/20130410/MILORL/gameinfo.html|archive-date=March 22, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> A week later, he scored a career-high 28 points in a 95–89 win over the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Rookie John Henson lifts Bucks past Kevin Durant-less Thunder|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400278946|access-date=March 18, 2016|work=ESPN.com|date=April 17, 2013}}</ref>

On October 19, 2013, the Bucks exercised their third-year team option on Henson's rookie scale contract, extending the contract through the 2014–15 season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Milwaukee Bucks exercise contract options on John Henson and Brandon Knight|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14587|access-date=October 19, 2013|work=InsideHoops.com|date=October 2, 2015}}</ref> In [[2013–14 NBA season|2013–14]], he averaged 11.1 points and 7.1 rebounds per game as he came off the bench in 47 of the 70 games he played.<ref>{{Cite web |title=John Henson Career Stats - NBA |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/stats/_/id/6592/index |access-date=2024-02-21 |website=ESPN |language=en}}</ref>

On October 16, 2014, the Bucks exercised their fourth-year team option on Henson's rookie scale contract, extending the contract through the 2015–16 season.<ref>{{cite news|title=BUCKS EXERCISE ROOKIE SCALE CONTRACT OPTIONS ON ANTETOKOUNMPO AND HENSON|url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/release/bucks-exercise-rookie-scale-contract-options-antetokounmpo-and-henson|access-date=October 16, 2014|work=NBA.com|date=October 2, 2015}}</ref> Henson played in 67 games for Milwaukee in 2014–15 (11 starts), averaging 7.0 points and 4.7 rebounds per game. He finished fifth in the league for blocks per game with 2.01 and became one of just seven players in Bucks history to average over 2.0 blocks in a single season. Henson blocked at least one shot in 20 straight games from December 26 to February 22, which was the third-longest streak during the 2014–15 season.<ref name=extension>{{cite news|title=BUCKS SIGN HENSON TO CONTRACT EXTENSION|url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/release/bucks-sign-henson-contract-extension|access-date=October 2, 2015|work=NBA.com|date=October 2, 2015}}</ref>

On October 2, 2015, Henson signed a four-year, $45 million contract extension with the Bucks.<ref name="extension" /><ref>{{cite news|last=Stein|first=Marc|title=John Henson agrees to four-year extension with Bucks|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/13792182/john-henson-agrees-four-year-extension-milwaukee-bucks|access-date=October 2, 2015|work=ESPN.com|date=October 2, 2015}}</ref> On November 6, 2015, in just his second game of the 2015–16 season, Henson scored a season-high 22 points off the bench in a 99–92 win over the [[New York Knicks]].<ref>{{cite news|title=John Henson 2015-16 Game Log|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/h/hensojo01/gamelog/2016/|access-date=March 18, 2016|work=Basketball-Reference.com}}</ref>

On October 29, 2016, Henson hit the game-winning buzzer-beater tip-in against the [[Brooklyn Nets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899481|title=Henson's tip-in at buzzer leads Bucks past Nets|work=ESPN.com|date=October 29, 2016|access-date=October 30, 2016}}</ref> In 21 minutes off the bench, he recorded 12 rebounds, seven points, three assists, two steals and two blocks in the 110–108 win.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=400899481|title=Nets vs. Bucks – Box Score|work=ESPN.com|date=October 29, 2016|access-date=October 30, 2016}}</ref> On November 27, 2016, he scored a season-high 20 points in 104–96 win over the Orlando Magic.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899698|title=Henson scores 20 as Bucks beat Magic, 104-96|work=ESPN.com|date=November 27, 2016|access-date=November 28, 2016}}</ref>

On February 4, 2018, Henson had season highs with 19 points and 18 rebounds in a 109–94 win over the [[Brooklyn Nets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975531|title=Giannis leaves early, but Bucks rout Nets 109-94|work=ESPN.com|date=February 4, 2018|access-date=February 4, 2018}}</ref>

On November 16, 2018, Henson was ruled out for approximately 12 weeks with a torn left wrist ligament.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/medical-updates-john-henson-and-donte-divincenzo|title=Medical Updates On John Henson And Donte DiVincenzo|work=NBA.com|date=November 16, 2018|access-date=November 16, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Velazquez|first=Matt|url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/nba/bucks/2018/11/16/henson-have-wrist-surgery-divincenzo-miss-least-three-games/2025319002/|title=John Henson to have wrist surgery, Donte DiVincenzo to miss at least three games|work=jsonline.com|date=November 16, 2018|access-date=November 16, 2018}}</ref> He underwent surgery on November 28.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/medical-update-john-henson|title=Medical Update On John Henson|work=NBA.com|date=November 28, 2018|access-date=November 28, 2018}}</ref>

===Cleveland Cavaliers (2018–2020)===
On December 7, 2018, Henson was traded, along with [[Matthew Dellavedova]] and the Bucks 2021 first and second round picks, to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in a five-player, three-team deal. The Cavs also received the [[Washington Wizards]] 2022 second round pick. The Bucks received [[George Hill (basketball)|George Hill]], [[Jason Smith (basketball, born 1986)|Jason Smith]] and a 2021 second round pick. The Wizards received [[Sam Dekker]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Cavaliers Acquire Matthew Dellavedova, John Henson and Three Future Draft Picks In Three-Team Trade|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/dellavedova-henson-trade-181207|access-date=December 8, 2018|work=NBA.com|date=December 7, 2018}}</ref>

===Detroit Pistons (2020)===
On February 6, 2020, the Cavaliers traded Henson, [[Brandon Knight (basketball)|Brandon Knight]], and a 2023 second round draft pick to the [[Detroit Pistons]] in exchange for [[Andre Drummond]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Detroit Pistons Acquire Brandon Knight, John Henson And Future Second Round Pick|url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/news/pistons-acquire-knight-henson|website=NBA.com|date=February 6, 2020|access-date=February 6, 2020}}</ref>

On April 5, 2021, the [[New York Knicks]] signed Henson to a 10-day contract;<ref>{{cite tweet|author=NY_KnicksPR|title=@nyknicks Sign C/F John Henson|number=1379177053673684997|user=NY_KnicksPR|date=April 5, 2021|access-date=April 6, 2021}}</ref> however, he did not see action with the team.

On March 8, 2022, Henson signed with [[Mets de Guaynabo (basketball)|Mets de Guaynabo]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Dario|last=Skerletic|title=John Henson joins Mets de Guaynabo|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/john-henson-joins-mets-de-guaynabo/|website=Sportando.basketball|date=March 9, 2022|access-date=March 10, 2022}}</ref> However, he didn't play any games with them.

On September 11, 2024, Henson announced his retirement.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Helin |first1=Kurt |title=Former Milwaukee player, North Carolina standout John Henson confirms his retirement from NBA |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nba/news/former-milwaukee-player-north-carolina-standout-john-henson-confirms-his-retirement-from-nba |website=NBC Sports |access-date=January 13, 2026 |date=September 11, 2024}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Henson is the son of Matt and Annette Henson. His father played basketball for [[Norfolk State Spartans football|Norfolk State University]].<ref name="thb" /> His sister, Amber, played basketball for [[Duke University]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Amber Henson Bio|url=http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=205184366|access-date=October 2, 2015|work=GoDuke.com}}</ref>

Henson is an ambassador for Up2Us Sports, a national non-profit organization dedicated to supporting underserved youth by providing them with coaches trained in positive youth development.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/more-sports/photos/2014/10/29/athletes-giving-back-2014|title=Athletes Giving Back|work=Sports Illustrated |date=October 29, 2014 |access-date=April 14, 2017}}</ref>
